title: Architectural Review Board approves 45 Glenn Road porch with added trim piece
text:
← Back to the wire

Architectural Review Board approves 45 Glenn Road porch with added trim piece
The board voted to approve the already-constructed project after asking the homeowner to add a cap trim detail at the top of the porch posts.
The Architectural Review Board on Thursday, Oct. 1, approved the front facade changes at 45 Glenn Road, a project that had already been built, on condition that a trim piece be added to the tops of the porch posts.
THE PROJECT Board members reviewed the case first during an earlier work session, noting that an earlier version of the porch design had not been approved. "It is an improvement over the previous versions," one board member said of the current design, adding that the porch roof was now co-planer with the main house roof.
Some members initially questioned whether the submitted photo was real. "I was like is this photo a really good photoshopped or is it constructed?" one board member asked, before confirming the porch was already built.
TRIM DETAIL During the public hearing, board members pointed to a drawing, sheet P-1, showing a trim piece at the top of the post where it meets the beam. A board member asked the applicant, identified only as Aaron, whether that detail could still be installed. "I was wondering if we might be able to install that, if you've got room to install that with what's already constructed," the board member said.
Aaron responded, "Oh, I'm sure I can put on whatever you guys decide." Aaron also confirmed trim already existed around the base of the posts.
THE VOTE A board member moved "to approve 45 Glenn Road with the addition of a trim piece at the post capital," and the motion was seconded. One member said "I oppose" during the vote. The project was approved as noted.
